newsitem.title: USA: Starbucks sees $170 mln capital expenses.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks sees $170 mln capital expenses.

text.p: Starbucks Corp on Wednesday said it expected to increase capital spending to about $170 million in the current fiscal year from $162 million in the year ended September 29, 1996.

Starbucks said in its annual report to shareholders it thought existing cash and investments plus cash generated from operations should cover the capital requirements for its core businesses in the current year.

In addition to the capital expenses associated with opening at least 325 stores in North America this year, up from 307 last year, Starbucks outlined cash requirements for another $24 million, mostly for its domestic joint ventures and international expansion.

Last year Starbucks invested $2.4 million in its Japanese joint venture with SAZABY Inc, $2.7 million in its joint venture with PepsiCo Inc and about $900,000 in a venture with Dreyer's Grand Ice Cream Inc, the company said.
The Pepsico venture includes a national rollout of bottled Frappuccino now planned for the summer of 1997, Starbucks executives said in a letter to shareholders.
Starbucks also said planned "cannibalization" and increased competition "may continue to put downward pressure on its comparable-store sales growth in future periods."
The company said that as of September 29 it had about $47 million in fixed-price commitments to purchase coffee, which it said would provide an adequate supply well into fiscal 1997.
